text:
incident-bot: Pager alert — increased SSE disconnects and tool-call parse errors detected on /v1/streaming endpoints (error rate spike @ 17:34 UTC). P50 latency normal, p95 token lag increased. Paging on-call (tag: #oncall).

maya: seeing same in dashboards. lots of CloudFront 499s in front of streaming backends, also tool-call failures reported by client SDKs.

aj: oncall here, looking now. assigning to devon for runtime logs. nina — can you start customer-impact estimate?

devon: grabbing logs. initial grep across runtime nodes:

```
2026-03-15T17:33:40Z runtime-23 tool_call_parser.go:142 error="tool_call_parse_error: unexpected EOF"
2026-03-15T17:33:41Z runtime-23 sse/conn.go:78 warning="client disconnected: remote: read timeout"
2026-03-15T17:33:42Z runtime-27 tool_call_parser.go:142 error="tool_call_parse_error: missing 'args' field"
2026-03-15T17:33:43Z runtime-19 sse/conn.go:120 info="retrying connection, seq=874"
```

devon: also correlating with deploy events — a canary of parser-worker v2.4.0 rolled out at 17:28 UTC (deploy-bot shows partial rollout to 10% nodes).

lucas: client telemetry shows malformed JSON fragments hitting the tool-call path from two SDK versions: js-sdk@1.5.0 and py-sdk@0.9.7, both recent.

nina: customer impact quick estimate — initial sampling: ~1.8% of active streaming sessions saw tool-call failures; approx 12 customers reported degraded behavior in last 30m, none on Dedicated (hosted API only). holding room for CP.

maya: mitigation idea — force fallback parser (v2.3.9) for streaming-toolcalls globally, and abort canary. can we flip config flag?

aj: agreed. devon, do we have a quick feature-flag kill switch? ops-bot, any automated rollback for canaries?

ops-bot: /rollback canary parser-worker v2.4.0 — initiated. will progressively shift traffic to v2.3.9 across 10 nodes/min.

devon: rolling back now. running a targeted restart on runtime-23/27/19 first. logs show parse errors drop after restart on node-23 (patched to v2.3.9):

```
2026-03-15T17:36:12Z runtime-23 tool_call_parser.go:info patched to v2.3.9
2026-03-15T17:36:15Z runtime-23 tool_call_parser.go:info parse-ok seq=879
```

maya: nice. timeline so far (for RCA thread):
- 17:28 UTC: parser-worker v2.4.0 canary -> 10% nodes
- 17:33 UTC: first spike of tool_call_parse_error and SSE disconnects
- 17:34 UTC: incident-bot pager triggered (automated)
- 17:35-17:38 UTC: rollback to v2.3.9 started
- 17:36 UTC: parse errors reduce on initial nodes
- 17:40 UTC: global rollback complete, client reports dropping

aj: good. hypothesis bank to track in this thread:
1) bug in v2.4.0 parser that mishandles streaming-toolcall fragments -> causes parse errors and connection churn
2) increased client-side fragmentation with new SDK versions (js-sdk@1.5.0) causing partial frames that the new parser didn't tolerate
3) downstream network/transcoding edge (CloudFront) injecting 499s independent of parser change

devon: evidence for (1) — errors point to parser code paths touched in v2.4.0 (diff includes stricter JSON validation). evidence for (2) — telemetry shows a bump in malformed payloads coincident with SDK rollouts; however malformed rate smaller than error spike. (3) less likely — 499s concentration maps to nodes running v2.4.0.

nina: customer impact note for ops: some customers saw session resets but most resumed after reconnect. no data exfil or PII exposure. flagged for account execs.

lucas: saving trace IDs for samples: trace-0ab3, trace-0ab7, trace-0ac5 (attached in S3 under s3://redwood-incident-logs/1710462022/)

maya: next steps — (A) confirm rollback fully removes errors for 1hr window, (B) gather more traces from affected SDK versions, (C) write post-incident test that fuzzes streaming-toolcall fragments against parser v2.4.0 and v2.3.9.

aj: handing off to nina for 17:50–18:20 UTC mid-shift for deeper RCA writeup. i'm still available if anything spikes.

nina: taking over. i'll collect logs, create timeline doc and assign action items. filing a JIRA: INF-4821 to track follow-ups (owner: devon). I'll ping when draft RCA is ready.

devon: note — we should capture kernel-level TCP resets from runtime nodes and CloudFront edge logs to be thorough. adding to INF-4821.

ops-bot: mitigation status: rollback complete at 17:40 UTC; monitoring retention set to 60m for streaming error rate.

maya: quick customer comm draft for accounts team:
"We observed a transient increase in streaming tool-call errors caused by a parser canary. We rolled back the canary within 12 minutes. Affected customers experienced session resets; services have recovered. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a detailed RCA and repro steps."

nina: copied to accounts. action items in-thread (simple tracker):
- [ ] INF-4821: collect all runtime logs (devon)
- [ ] Fuzz test for parser fragment handling (devon + lucas)
- [ ] SDK telemetry analysis (client-eng)
- [ ] Postmortem writeup (nina)
- [ ] Add e2e regression test to CI for streaming-toolcall (maya)

lucas: adding note — reproducible locally with js-sdk@1.5.0 when sending split frames with no `args` field; will attach minimal repro snippet to JIRA.

aj: thanks all. leaving this in nina's hands for RCA consolidation. if error rate rises again, page me immediately.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated by rollback at 17:40 UTC. Incident opened: 1710462022. Severity: Sev3 -> will schedule postmortem.

nina: draft RCA will be posted to #incidents-docs and linked here when ready. closing active paging for now.
